notes: EIGHT BLOCKS, AND NO code_section. This page has eight `sections` rows — why, what, process,
alternatives, technology, investment, gallery, faq — in exactly the order of its eight
template bands, and it draws no <LocalTrust>, so there is no bespoke band to hold a place
for and nothing is added to vs-content-model.php or CodeSectionBlock.astro.
BAND VOCABULARY IS READ OFF sinus-lift.css AND THE TEMPLATE'S OWN COMMENTS WERE WRONG. The
band comments in the .astro said "cream split" for #what and #technology and "sage" for
#process and #gallery. All four were wrong: `.section.alt` is CHARCOAL
(sinus-lift.css:225 -> var(--vs-charcoal-green), h2 #fff at :226-229, p rgba(255,255,255,0.85)
at :233) and `.section.dark` is SAGE-PALE (sinus-lift.css:235 -> var(--vs-sage-pale), h2
var(--vs-ink) at :236-239). `sage` and `sage-pale` are two separate BLOCK_BANDS choices
painting two different tokens, and `alt` means cream on teeth-whitening.css:237 — so a value
copied from a sibling, or trusted from the comment above the band, repaints four of these
eight bands. Each `band_evidence` names the rule it was read from, and the comments in the
template were corrected in the same change as this file.
THIS PAGE'S `cards` REPEATER HOLDS 13 ROWS IN FOUR GROUPS AND THE TEMPLATE READS NONE OF
THEM. causeCards (4), alternatives (3), techList (3) and costBullets (3) all exist in the
live CMS — verified — while sinus-lift.astro declares four const arrays with the identical
copy and renders those instead. So three of the four groups are MOVED by the blocks below
rather than transcribed, and the migration quietly fixes a divergence: after the backfill
the alternatives, tech list and cost factors come from wp-admin, which is where an editor
has always been able to change them and where changing them has so far had no effect.
causeCards is the one group nothing can claim — see `exempt.cards`.
THREE BANDS LOSE SOMETHING AND ALL THREE LOSSES ARE STRUCTURAL, NOT COPY-SHAPED.
#why    — the three-cell `.why-creds` strip (600+ hrs / 300+ reviews / Implant Pathway).
#what   — the entire `.what-sub` "Common Causes" sub-grid: an eyebrow, an <h3>, a
paragraph and four `.cause-card`s.
#investment — the two-column `.invest-grid` and the whole sage `.insurance-card` aside.
Each is written out in full in `known_gaps` on its block, with what would close it. Nothing
was invented to cover them, no field was added, and no layout was proposed.
THE FAQ BAND SPLITS body/pull THE OTHER WAY FROM porcelain-veneers, and this is the single
easiest thing to get wrong by pattern-matching. Here the CMS `faq` row's body IS the
section-head paragraph (sinus-lift.astro:654) and the `.pull` aside is hardcoded
(:673-679). On porcelain-veneers the head has no paragraph and the CMS body is the pull.
Copying that route's mapping would move the head's paragraph into the aside and leave the
head bare.
THE RAIL IS SEVEN ENTRIES AND THE BLOCK LIST IS EIGHT. The live toc_links run why, what,
process, alternatives, technology, investment, faq — `gallery` has no row and stays out of
the rail, which is where it is today. Block order is template order and template order is
the rail's order, so no rail entry moves.
CTA ROWS SPLIT THE SAME TWO WAYS AS BOTH WORKED EXAMPLES, and the split is the components'
decision, not this file's. `alternatives` and `process` draw their rows entirely from the
component — comparison_cards has no cta sub-fields and process_steps' inline-cta buttons are
site data from src/data/contact.ts — so nothing is supplied for them; `what` and `faq` gate
their row on cta_label being filled, so those two carry a transcribed pair. All eight
`sections` rows on this page return ctaLabel and ctaHref null — verified live — so there was
never anything to move.

blocks.band_evidence: sinus-lift.astro:308 <section class="section"> — .sinuslift .section (sinus-lift.css:224) sets padding: 110px 0 and nothing else, no background, so the body paper shows through (global.css:25, body background-color: var(--vs-paper), and --vs-paper is #ffffff at tokens.css:12).
blocks.layout_evidence: .why-image precedes .why-text in the DOM (sinus-lift.astro:311, 319), so the photo is on the LEFT and `media_side` is `left` — which selects MediaSplitBlock's `.what-*` family (MediaSplitBlock.astro:275-276). The band has no CTA row and no pull quote, so no cta or quote sub-field is supplied.
ratio_is_even_on_purpose: the layout offers is `wide-text`, which is `1fr 1.1fr` — but the page sheet's own
(0,2,0), the SAME specificity as the block's `.what-grid.ratio-wide-text`, and file
order between a page stylesheet and a component's scoped styles is not guaranteed. So
`wide-text` would render 1fr 1.1fr or 1fr 1fr depending on link order.
`even` is chosen instead because it emits no modifier at all and both sheets then agree
on 1fr 1fr. A deterministic 1fr 1fr is worth more than a marginally closer value that
two stylesheets are racing for — and the difference from 0.9fr 1.1fr is named as a gap
below rather than hidden inside a cascade.
blocks.image_alt_note: The images row for slot drRichardsonImg carries alt "Dr. Bryce Richardson, lead surgeon at Vivid Smiles Dentistry in Parker, CO" — confirmed live, and character-for-character the string the template hardcodes at sinus-lift.astro:314. Moved, not transcribed: the row exists.
blocks.eyebrow_note: The CMS `why` row holds eyebrow "Why Vivid Smiles", heading and body all non-null — verified live — and the template reads all three (sinus-lift.astro:320-322). Nothing here is a literal.
known_gaps: THE THREE-CELL `.why-creds` STRIP IS LOST. This is the largest loss on this route.
sinus-lift.astro:323-338 is `.why-creds` — a three-column band under the lede, ruled off
with a border-top, holding three `.cred` cells:
600+ hrs        / Advanced Surgical Training
300+ ★★★★★      / Five-Star Google Reviews
Implant Pathway / Clinical Staff Role
Six short strings and one inline star run. No registered layout has a repeater of
figure-plus-label pairs: `stat_callout` carries exactly ONE figure (`value` + `unit` +
`caption`), which is why it is not the layout for this band — the band is three, not
one, and folding two of them away to fit would delete two of the practice's three
credentials. `card_grid` could hold three cards but only by giving up the photograph
and the editorial split, which is more of the band than the strip is.
WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a `stats { value unit caption }` repeater on `media_split`, drawn
by MediaSplitBlock as `.why-creds > .cred > .cred-stat + .cred-label` after the prose
— the same shape `checklist` got when four pages needed `.candidate-list`. It is one
repeater and one template branch, and three of the eight implant pages carry a
credentials strip of this shape. Adding it is a component change, not a page change.
THE PHOTO'S BOX CHANGES ORIENTATION, AND IT IS THE MOST VISIBLE OF THESE.
`.sinuslift .why-image` is `aspect-ratio: 4/5` (sinus-lift.css:280) — a portrait plate.
MediaSplitBlock's left-hand plate is `.what-img`, `aspect-ratio: 5/4`
(MediaSplitBlock.astro's style block, `.what-img`), and the page sheet's own
`.sinuslift .what-img` is 5/4 too (sinus-lift.css:347), so both agree on landscape.
The source file is 1200x1800 — portrait — so `object-fit: cover` will crop it hard,
top and bottom, to fill a landscape box.
WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the family's five differences travel together by design
(MediaSplitBlock's header sets that out at length), so the fix is NOT a per-band
aspect field — it is `media_side: right`, which selects `.natural-*` and gives a 4/5
portrait plate. That is not taken here because it also puts the text first and the
photo on the right, inverting the band's DOM order and its visual composition. Which
of the two is the smaller loss is a design call, and it is recorded here rather than
made unilaterally in a migration.
SMALLER, AND LISTED SO NOBODY RE-DISCOVERS THEM:
- Column tracks go from 0.9fr 1.1fr to 1fr 1fr. See
`ratio_is_even_on_purpose` above for why the nearer value was refused.
- The wrappers are renamed: `.why-editorial` -> `.what-grid`, `.why-image` ->
`.what-img`, `.why-text` -> `.what-text`. The block carries its own declarations
for its own names, and the gap 80px and align-items: center match, so the change
is in the class attribute rather than in the rendering.
- `p.why-lede` becomes `.prose > p`, so the lede's own treatment
(17px / line-height 1.85 / max-width 56ch, sinus-lift.css:302-305) is replaced by
the block's paragraph treatment. `.sinuslift .why-lede strong` (:306-309) goes with
it, but the CMS body carries no <strong>, so nothing rendered changes there.

known_gaps: THE ENTIRE `.what-sub` "COMMON CAUSES" SUB-GRID IS LOST, AND IT IS ROUGHLY HALF THIS
BAND.
sinus-lift.astro:380-400 hangs a second, self-contained unit off the bottom of the
media split, inside the same <section id="what">:
- `.what-sub-head` — eyebrow "Common Causes", an <h3> "Why You Might Need a Sinus
Lift for Dental Implants", and a paragraph of prose (:382-394).
- `.cause-grid` — four `.cause-card`s, each a `.tag` over an <h4>: Most common /
Upper back tooth loss, Cause / Periodontal disease, Cause / Long-term denture wear,
Cause / Naturally thin sinus anatomy (:393-400).
The four cards ARE in the CMS as the `causeCards` group — see `exempt.cards`, where they
are excused rather than dropped silently — but there is nowhere on `media_split` to put
them and no way to reach them: the layout has one image, one copy column, one optional
quote, one optional checklist, one optional aside and two buttons, and none of those is
a four-card grid with its own heading.
WHY THIS IS NOT SOLVED BY SPLITTING THE BAND IN TWO. A `card_grid` block after this one
would draw the four cards, but as a SECOND <section> with its own band padding and its
own id — where the page has one section, one 110px band and one `#what` anchor. That
changes the page's structure and its rail target to save a mapping, which is the
opposite of the rule this file is written to.
WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: a `sub_cards { meta title }` repeater plus `sub_eyebrow`,
`sub_heading` and `sub_body` on `media_split`, drawn by MediaSplitBlock after the grid
as `.what-sub > .what-sub-head + .cause-grid`. The repeater name must not be `cards`,
`tiers`, `items`, `points`, `steps`, `checklist`, `plans` or `features` — every one of
those is already minted by another layout in `blocks`, and a shared repeater name
merges the two GraphQL types and silently drops one side's sub-fields
(vs-content-model.php:539-541, and manifest.ts says the same at the pricing_tiers
entry). `sub_cards` collides with none of them.

known_gaps: THE CARD SHELL IS RENAMED AND SLIGHTLY RESIZED. Content-complete; geometry is not.
This page spells the shape `.alt-grid` / `.alt-card` (sinus-lift.css:452-483);
ComparisonCardsBlock spells it `.compare` / `.compare-card` and carries its own
declarations for those names. The page's `.alt-*` rules go unused on the backfilled
band. Measured differences, page value first:
grid gap        24px  ->  22px
grid max-width  1180px with margin: 0 auto  ->  no cap, full .wrap width
card padding    38px 34px 34px  ->  36px 32px 32px
Everything else matches: repeat(3, 1fr), 1px var(--vs-line) border, var(--vs-r-lg)
radius, the translateY(-3px) hover, and the card background — `#fff` on this page and
`var(--vs-paper)` in the block, which is #ffffff at tokens.css:12.
WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the same treatment #technology's list gets — an additive alias in
sinus-lift.css giving `.sinuslift .compare` and `.sinuslift .compare-card` this page's
three values, deleting nothing, so `.alt-*` stays for the else branch. It is NOT done
here, and the difference between the two cases is worth stating: `.tech-list` and
`.candidate-list` are the same declarations character for character in all four sheets
that carry them, so an alias there cannot change a rendered pixel. These three values
differ, so an alias here would override the block's own geometry from a page sheet and
make this one band render unlike every other comparison_cards band on the site. That
is a design decision about which of the two shapes is correct, and it belongs to
whoever owns the design system, not to a migration.

checklist.note: All 3 rows of the `techList` cards group, in order — verified live — with the bolded lead-in zipped on from the map. `item` is the CMS row's body; `lead` is what the template actually puts inside the , which is the row's title plus a trailing space and em dash (sinus-lift.astro:517, `{t.title} —`).
why_lead_is_zipped_and_not_mapped: `lead` could have been mapped straight off the card's `title`, and that would have
printed "CBCT imaging Gives Dr. Richardson…" — the em dash gone and the
sentence running straight on. The dash is not decoration: it is what separates the
term from its definition on every line of this list and on the `.candidate-list`s of
the three sibling implant pages, and MediaSplitBlock's `lead` is documented as
carrying its own dash for exactly that reason.
So the row is assembled the way row_kinds describes for a list whose text lives in
the CMS but whose labels live in the template: the sentence is moved, the lead-in is
zipped on positionally, and the backfill refuses the pairing outright if the group
ever stops being three rows long. The three lead strings are transcription of what
checklist.markers_are_derived: The template's 01/02/03 come from the `marker` key on the const array (sinus-lift.astro:88-104, printed at :515). They are NOT transcribed: MediaSplitBlock computes the marker from row position, so a reorder in wp-admin cannot leave the numbering out of sequence. The three stored values happen to be 01/02/03 in order, so the rendered numerals are unchanged.

closed_gaps: THE CLASS-NAME SPLIT BETWEEN `.tech-list` AND `.candidate-list` IS CLOSED, IN THE PAGE
MediaSplitBlock draws its checklist as `ul.candidate-list` — one class for a shape three
sibling implant pages already spell that way and this one spells `.tech-list`. The five
rules behind the two names are the same declarations character for character, which
MediaSplitBlock's own header states and which was re-read against sinus-lift.css:515-534
sinus-lift.css now carries `.sinuslift .candidate-list` and its four descendants with
those same five rules, copied not grouped, and `.tech-list` is untouched — it is what
the else branch still emits, and deleting it would take the rollback path with it.
Because the values are identical on both sides, it does not matter which of the page
`.section.alt .candidate-list .marker` wins the cascade; both resolve to
What the alias actually buys is not the rendering — the block would render correctly
without it — but that THIS sheet goes on describing this band. Without it, a designer
editing `.tech-list` after the backfill would change nothing and have no way to see why.
known_gaps: NONE. Photo, eyebrow, heading, pull quote and all three list lines have a field, the
markers are derived, and the band has no prose column, no aside and no CTA row for
anything to be lost from. See `quote_cascade_note` for two colour declarations that
resolve to the block's values; they are a difference of a few percent of alpha, not a
loss of content.
